# Usage Examples

BergAgents has three surfaces over the same Harness engine: the TUI, the Python API, and the web UI.

## TUI

```bash
python -m berg_agents --tui
```

Bare text runs a `generic` task; `/harness` (alias `/task`) runs it with explicit `harness` task type:

```
harness> refactor the login flow to use sessions
harness> /harness add retry logic to the sync worker
harness> /agents
harness> /stats
harness> /help
```

Slash commands (identical list and order in the web picker):

| Command     | What it does                   |
  |-------------|--------------------------------|
| `/help`     | Show all slash commands        |
| `/agents`   | List registered agents         |
| `/models`   | Show available models (web UI) |
| `/stats`    | Learning statistics            |
| `/tools`    | List available tools (web UI)  |
| `/health`   | System health check (web UI)   |
| `/history`  | Show session task transcript   |
| `/memory`   | Memory information (web UI)    |
| `/context`  | Show current context (web UI)  |
| `/settings` | Show settings (web UI)         |
| `/plugins`  | List plugins (web UI)          |
| `/skills`   | List skills (web UI)           |
| `/mcps`     | MCP server status (web UI)     |
| `/harness`  | Run a task through the harness |
| `/task`     | Same as `/harness`             |
| `/clear`    | Clear the session              |

Commands marked "web UI" are listed in the TUI for parity but answered there with a web-only notice.
Unknown commands warn and continue.

## Web UI

```bash
python -m berg_agents --web --port 8001
# → http://127.0.0.1:8001
```

Type `/` to open the slash-command picker (same 16 commands as the TUI).
Agent, HITL, and learning panels update from the same task lifecycle the TUI renders.

### Frontend development

For UI work, run the backend and the Next.js dev server separately.
The dev server is cross-origin, so it needs the backend URL at startup (inlined by Next.js) - without it all `/api/*`
calls 404 against
Next.js itself.
The backend allows CORS from `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`
ports 3000-3001.

```bash
python -m berg_agents --web --port 8001   # backend API
cd berg_agents/ui/webapp && NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8001 npm run dev
# → http://localhost:3001 (3000 if free)
```

Production needs none of this: `python -m berg_agents --web` serves the
API and the static Next.js build from one origin.

## Human-in-the-Loop

When a task needs review, the Harness returns `needs_human_review`:

- **TUI**: the result panel shows the review reasons, then `Approve and resume? [y/N]:` - approval re-executes with
  `hitl_decision: approve` in metadata, anything else fails the task as rejected.
- **Web**: the HITL surface shows tool name + arguments with Approve / Reject / Edit (edit rewrites the args before the
  tool runs).

See [Tools](TOOLS.qmd) for which tools pause by default.
